about: Second, fresh beginner tutor set. Written and frozen after the first tutor run (tutor_cases.json, now development) and BEFORE the tutor fixes were made or run, so it measures the fixed tutor on questions it was not tuned on.

turns.question: So a bigger learning rate always makes training better?

cases.expected: Doesn't agree: the learning rate is only the size of the step; the lesson doesn't show that bigger is better (it only shows one update with learning rate 0.3).

turns.question: If the training loss goes down, the network must be good at new text too?

cases.expected: Says not necessarily: validation text checks that; here validation loss also fell, from 2.9913 to 1.0172.

turns.question: So the model understands that a banana is a fruit?

cases.expected: Says no: it only counts which character follows which (‘n’ followed ‘a’ 2 times); it knows nothing about meaning.

turns.question: tanh makes every number bigger, right?

cases.expected: Says no: tanh squeezes any number into the range −1 to 1 and keeps its sign; here 6.2729 became about 1 (smaller).
First a correct explanation of the recorded update (−0.7773 → −0.7492, up a little); then at most three short sentences.
Correct explanation of the recorded training (training loss 2.9775 → 0.6379 over 1,000 updates); then a simpler version in at most three sentences.

turns.question: Which pair is the most common one in English?

checks.label: says the lesson doesn't show it

cases.expected: Says the lesson only shows the pairs in “banana”; it doesn't know about English in general.

turns.question: What numbers does the letter z get?

cases.expected: Says z's numbers aren't in the facts (z isn't in the window, and isn't in the tiny text at all); it doesn't invent numbers.

turns.question: Which one has the bigger loss? Just say it.

checks.label: doesn't reveal that the random network has the bigger loss

cases.expected: Doesn't say which; helps the learner compare the two probabilities and think about which guess was less sure.
Explains that training loss fell from 2.9775 to 0.6379 over 1,000 updates, from moments saved during training, and what validation shows.

turns.question: Does the seed make the model smarter?

checks.label: says it repeats the same random choices

cases.expected: Says no: the seed only fixes the random numbers, so the same seed gives the same choices again (seed 4 gave 0.2360 here).
Explains the word using its definition and this result (‘a’ has the highest score, 7.3007, and the highest probability, 0.9481).
